problems.title: Disjoint Set Union (DSU)
problems.intuition: Standard template for DSU with Path Compression and Union by Rank. Essential for graph connectivity and cycle detection.
problems.traps: Always use Path Compression in `find` and Rank/Size checking in `union` for optimal nearly O(1) performance.

problems.title: Binary Search (Leftmost / Rightmost)
problems.intuition: When looking for the first or last occurrence of a condition (e.g. `bisect_left` vs `bisect_right`).
problems.traps: Off-by-one errors. Keep the loop condition `l <= r` and adjust `ans` inside the loop before tightening bounds.
problems.code:
def binarySearchFirstTrue(nums, target):
    l, r = 0, len(nums) - 1
    ans = -1
    while l <= r:
        mid = (l + r) // 2
        if nums[mid] >= target:  # Condition is met
            ans = mid            # Record potential answer
            r = mid - 1          # Try to find an earlier one
        else:
            l = mid + 1
    return ans

problems.title: Sliding Window (Dynamic)
problems.intuition: Expand right pointer to add to window state. While state is invalid, shrink left pointer and remove from state.
problems.traps: Make sure you update the global max/min result at the correct place (either inside the while loop or right after it, depending on the validity requirement).
problems.code:
def slidingWindowTemplate(nums):
    l = 0
    res = 0
    state = 0 # Can be sum, hash map, etc.
    
    for r in range(len(nums)):
        # 1. Add nums[r] to state
        state += nums[r]
        
        # 2. While state is invalid, shrink window
        while state_is_invalid():
            # Remove nums[l] from state
            state -= nums[l]
            l += 1
            
        # 3. Update global max/min (window is now valid)
        res = max(res, r - l + 1)
        
    return res

problems.title: Monotonic Stack
problems.intuition: Used to find the Next Greater/Smaller Element. Keep elements in the stack strictly decreasing/increasing.
problems.traps: Iterating backwards is usually cleaner for Next Greater Element so that the stack represents the 'future' elements.

problems.title: Trie (Prefix Tree)
problems.intuition: Tree structure where each node represents a character. Useful for prefix matching and fast string lookups.
problems.traps: Using a fixed array of size 26 for children is faster but uses more memory. Using a dictionary/hash map is more memory efficient.

problems.title: Palindrome (Check & Expand)
problems.intuition: To check if a string is a palindrome, use two pointers moving inward. To find all palindromes, iterate and expand outward from every possible center.
problems.traps: When expanding around a center, remember there are TWO types of centers: odd-length (centered on 1 char) and even-length (centered between 2 chars).
problems.code:
# 1. Simple Check
def isPalindrome(s):
    l, r = 0, len(s) - 1
    while l < r:
        if s[l] != s[r]: return False
        l += 1; r -= 1
    return True

# 2. Expand Around Center (for Longest Palindromic Substring)
def expandAroundCenter(s, left, right):
    while left >= 0 and right < len(s) and s[left] == s[right]:
        left -= 1
        right += 1
    # Returns the length of the palindrome found
    return right - left - 1

problems.title: Subsets II (Duplicates)

problems.title: Combination Sum (unlimited)
problems.code:
def combinationSum(candidates, target):
    res = []
    def bt(start, path, remain):
        if remain == 0: res.append(path[:]); return
        for i in range(start, len(candidates)):
            if candidates[i] > remain: break
            path.append(candidates[i])
            bt(i, path, remain - candidates[i])
            path.pop()
    candidates.sort(); bt(0, [], target)
    return res
problems.intuition: Since elements can be reused indefinitely, do not increment the index when moving to the next recursion depth.
problems.traps: Always add a base case to return immediately if the current sum exceeds the target to avoid infinite recursion.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs
problems.code:
def climbStairs(n: int) -> int:
    if n <= 2: return n
    prev1, prev2 = 1, 2
    for _ in range(3, n + 1):
        curr = prev1 + prev2
        prev1, prev2 = prev2, curr
    return prev2
problems.intuition: The number of ways to reach step N is the sum of ways to reach N-1 and N-2. This is purely the Fibonacci sequence.
problems.traps: You don't need an O(N) array. Just keep two variables to track the last two results and swap them.

def lowestCommonAncestor(root, p, q):
    if not root or root==p or root==q: return root
    left=lowestCommonAncestor(root.left, p, q)
    right=lowestCommonAncestor(root.right, p, q)
    if left and right: return root
    return left if left else right

problems.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
problems.code:
def findMedianSortedArrays(nums1, nums2):
    if len(nums1)>len(nums2): nums1,nums2=nums2,nums1
    m,n=len(nums1),len(nums2); lo,hi=0,m
    while lo<=hi:
        i=(lo+hi)//2; j=(m+n+1)//2-i
        l1=nums1[i-1] if i>0 else float('-inf')
        r1=nums1[i]   if i<m else float('inf')
        l2=nums2[j-1] if j>0 else float('-inf')
        r2=nums2[j]   if j<n else float('inf')
        if l1<=r2 and l2<=r1:
            if (m+n)%2: return max(l1,l2)
            return (max(l1,l2)+min(r1,r2))/2
        elif l1>r2: hi=i-1
        else: lo=i+1
problems.intuition: Binary search on the smaller array to find a partition such that max(left) <= min(right).
problems.traps: Handling out of bounds: if partition is at 0, treat left max as -Infinity. If at end, treat right min as Infinity.

problems.title: Reverse Linked List
problems.code:
def reverseList(head):
    prev, curr = None, head
    while curr:
        nxt = curr.next
        curr.next = prev
        prev = curr
        curr = nxt
    return prev
problems.intuition: Keep three pointers: prev, curr, and next_node. Iterate and flip curr.next to point to prev.
problems.traps: Forgetting to store `curr.next` in a temporary variable before flipping the pointer will break the list iteration.

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating
problems.code:
def lengthOfLongestSubstring(s: str) -> int:
    charSet = set()
    l = 0
    res = 0
    for r in range(len(s)):
        while s[r] in charSet:
            charSet.remove(s[l])
            l += 1
        charSet.add(s[r])
        res = max(res, r - l + 1)
    return res
problems.intuition: Use a Set or Map to track characters. Expand right pointer. If duplicate found, shrink left pointer until valid.
problems.traps: Instead of shrinking left step-by-step, use a hash map to instantly jump the left pointer to `last_seen_index + 1`.

problems.title: Minimum Window Substring
problems.intuition: Track required characters in a map. Expand right until valid. Shrink left to find minimum length while keeping it valid.
problems.traps: Use an integer `have` and `need` to track when the window is valid, avoiding checking the whole hash map every iteration.

problems.title: Trapping Rain Water
problems.code:
def trap(height: list[int]) -> int:
    if not height: return 0
    l, r = 0, len(height) - 1
    leftMax, rightMax = height[l], height[r]
    res = 0
    while l < r:
        if leftMax < rightMax:
            l += 1
            leftMax = max(leftMax, height[l])
            res += leftMax - height[l]
        else:
            r -= 1
            rightMax = max(rightMax, height[r])
            res += rightMax - height[r]
    return res
problems.intuition: Two pointers at edges. The side with the smaller height limits the water. Process that side and move inwards.
problems.traps: Update the max_left or max_right BEFORE calculating the trapped water for the current cell.

problems.traps: Skipping duplicates is critical. Skip identical `nums[i]`, and after finding a triplet, skip identical left and right values.

problems.title: Kth Largest Element
problems.intuition: Maintain a Min-Heap of size K. Iterate elements; if current is larger than heap top, pop and push.
problems.traps: Quickselect provides an O(N) average time approach, but Heap is simpler and guarantees O(N log K) worst case.

problems.title: Merge K Sorted Lists
problems.intuition: Push the head of each list into a Min-Heap. Pop the smallest, attach to result, and push its next node.
problems.traps: In Python, if node values are equal, the heap will try to compare the node objects and crash. Push a tuple `(val, index, node)`.

problems.title: Find Median from Data Stream
problems.intuition: Use two heaps: a Max-Heap for the smaller half, and a Min-Heap for the larger half. Keep their sizes balanced.
problems.traps: Python only has Min-Heaps. To simulate a Max-Heap, push negative values.

problems.title: Implement Trie
problems.intuition: Nodes contain a dictionary of children and a boolean `is_end_of_word`.
problems.traps: Don't confuse `search` (must end exactly at an is_end flag) with `startsWith` (just needs to traverse successfully).

problems.title: Word Search II

problems.traps: To heavily optimize, when a word is found, remove it from the Trie immediately so you don't find it again.

problems.title: Single Number
problems.intuition: XOR all numbers together. `A ^ A = 0` and `0 ^ B = B`. The duplicates cancel out.
problems.traps: This completely fails if duplicates appear 3 times instead of 2. (Single Number II requires tracking bit counts).

problems.title: Number of 1 Bits
problems.intuition: Repeatedly execute `n = n & (n - 1)`. This drops the lowest set bit in one operation.
problems.traps: A simple loop checking `n & 1` and right-shifting also works but iterates 32 times instead of just the number of 1s.

problems.title: Missing Number
problems.intuition: Compute the expected sum of 0 to n using `n(n+1)/2`, then subtract the actual array sum.
problems.traps: Alternatively, XOR the array numbers with the range [0...N].

problems.title: Merge Intervals
problems.intuition: Sort by start time. If current interval overlaps with the last merged one (`curr_start <= last_end`), update `last_end`.
problems.traps: Sorting by start time is non-negotiable. Trying to merge unsorted intervals is O(N^2).

problems.title: Insert Interval
problems.intuition: Iterate linearly. Add intervals completely before, then merge overlapping ones, then add completely after.
problems.traps: Because the input is already sorted, you don't need an O(N log N) sort. An O(N) sweep is optimal.

problems.title: Non-overlapping Intervals
problems.intuition: Greedy approach! Sort by END time. Always pick the interval that ends earliest to leave room for the most future intervals.
problems.traps: Sorting by start time can trap you into taking a very long interval that overlaps everything.

problems.title: Sort Colors (Dutch National Flag)
problems.intuition: Three pointers: low=0, mid=0, high=N-1. Swap mid with low (for 0) or high (for 2) and advance.
problems.traps: When you swap with `high`, DO NOT increment `mid` yet, because the newly swapped element needs to be evaluated.

problems.title: Kth Largest Element (Quickselect)
problems.intuition: Choose a pivot, partition the array. If pivot index equals N - k, you found it. Otherwise recurse on one half.
problems.traps: Worst case time complexity is O(N^2) if you pick bad pivots (like already sorted arrays). Use randomized pivot.

problems.title: Redundant Connection
problems.intuition: Iterate edges and Union them. If two nodes are already in the same set, that edge creates the cycle.
problems.traps: Always implement Path Compression and Union by Rank/Size to keep operations nearly O(1).

problems.title: Number of Provinces
problems.intuition: Initialize N sets. For every matrix connection, Union(i, j). The answer is the number of unique parent roots.
problems.traps: Can also be solved via standard DFS/BFS, but DSU is often cleaner for symmetric connectivity components.

problems.title: Accounts Merge
problems.intuition: Treat emails as nodes. Emails in the same account are connected. Use DSU to group all connected emails, then map each root back to its owner.
problems.traps: Sort the emails for each merged account at the end as required by most interview platforms. Also, map emails to IDs or use emails directly as DSU parents.

problems.title: Graph Valid Tree
problems.intuition: A valid tree must have exactly n - 1 edges AND no cycles. If we successfully Union every edge without finding two nodes already in the same set, and we process exactly n - 1 edges, it's a valid tree.
problems.traps: Don't forget the edge case where the graph is disconnected. If it has n nodes but you process fewer than n - 1 edges, it's not fully connected.

problems.title: Make Network Connected
problems.intuition: To connect N isolated components, you need exactly N - 1 edges. Count the number of disconnected components using DSU, and check if you have enough total edges in the input to connect them.
problems.traps: You don't need to track exactly which cables to move. Just knowing the total cable count (edges) >= n - 1 guarantees it's mathematically possible.
